questions.stem: A clinic in Europe/London books each follow-up call with `visit.plus(Duration.ofDays(1))`. The UK clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00 in the early hours of Sunday 25 October 2026. When is the follow-up for a visit at 15:00 on Saturday 24 October?

options.text: 15:00 on Sunday, since a ZonedDateTime moves a day's worth of time to the same clock time on the next date
options.says: Duration.ofDays(1) is 86,400 seconds; adding it moves the instant, and only a Period or plusDays keeps the wall-clock time

options.text: 15:00 on Sunday, since Duration.ofDays counts a calendar day and leaves the hours to the zone rules
options.says: Duration.ofDays(1) is 24 hours of elapsed time, not a calendar day

options.text: 14:00 on Sunday, since 24 hours after the visit the clocks show an hour less than on Saturday
options.says: 24 elapsed hours after 15:00 BST is 14:00 GMT, because Sunday 25 October has 25 hours

options.text: 16:00 on Sunday, since 24 hours after the visit the clocks show an hour more than on Saturday
options.says: the clocks went back, so 24 hours later they read one hour earlier, not later

origin.section: Duration.ofDays(1) Is 24 Hours; Period.ofDays(1) Is the Next Calendar Day

questions.stem: A subscription started on 20 November 2025. A dashboard shows its days active on 5 January 2026 as `Period.between(started, today).getDays()`. What does it show?

options.text: 46, since getDays() gives the whole span between the two dates counted in days
options.says: getDays() is only the days field of P1M16D; the total, 46, comes from ChronoUnit.DAYS.between

options.text: 45, since getDays() gives the whole span between the two dates minus the start day
options.says: getDays() is only the days field of P1M16D, not any form of the total; ChronoUnit.DAYS.between gives the total, 46

options.text: 16, since getDays() gives what is left over after the whole months between the dates
options.says: Period.between gives P1M16D: one whole month to 20 December, then 16 days; getDays() is the 16

options.text: 15, since getDays() gives what is left over after counting each month as thirty days
options.says: Period.between counts real calendar months, not 30-day blocks

origin.section: Period.between Returns Fields; Count Days With ChronoUnit.DAYS.between

questions.stem: A billing rule gives a discount when `term.equals(Period.ofYears(1))`. A partner's file sets one customer's term to `P12M`, read with `Period.parse`. Does that customer get the discount?

options.text: Yes, since equals compares how long the two terms are, and twelve months make a year
options.says: Period.equals compares the year, month and day fields one by one, and P12M has 0 years and 12 months

options.text: Yes, since Period.parse folds the months into years as it reads the text
options.says: a Period keeps the fields it was given; parse does not normalize, only normalized() folds months into years

options.text: No, since equals compares the stored fields, and twelve months are not one year there
options.says: P12M and P1Y have different fields; they compare equal only after normalized()

options.text: No, since Period.parse reads the M in P12M as minutes, which a Period cannot hold
options.says: M before a T is months; minutes are written after the T, and Period.parse refuses any time part

origin.section: A Period Keeps the Fields It Was Given, So P14M Is Not P1Y2M

questions.stem: A race timer shows how far a runner is ahead of the target pace with `String.format("%d min %d s", d.toMinutes(), d.toSecondsPart())`. A runner is 75 seconds behind, so d is `Duration.ofSeconds(-75)`. What does the timer show?

options.text: -1 min 15 s, since only the minutes of a negative Duration carry its sign
options.says: every part of a negative Duration is negative, toSecondsPart() included

options.text: -2 min 45 s, since the parts of a Duration are rounded down to whole minutes first
options.says: toMinutes() truncates toward zero, giving -1, and toSecondsPart() is -15

options.text: -1 min -15 s, since the minutes and the seconds of a negative Duration both carry its sign
options.says: in a negative Duration toMinutes() and toSecondsPart() are both negative: -1 and -15

options.text: 1 min 15 s, since the minutes and the seconds of a Duration are sizes without a sign
options.says: the parts keep the sign; only abs() removes it

origin.section: Duration Prints Hours, Not Days, and Its Hours and Minutes Carry the Sign
